newsitem.title: CHINA: China opens foreign ministry commission in HK.
newsitem.headline: China opens foreign ministry commission in HK.

text.p: China's foreign ministry unveiled its office in Hong Kong on Tuesday to handle the territory's external affairs and serve as a channel to the central government in Beijing.
China's foreign minister Qian Qichen, Hong Kong's new leader Tung Chee-hwa and China's special envoy to the region Ma Yu Zhen opened the office, called the Office of the Commissioner.
Britain handed Hong Kong, its colony of 156 years, back to China at midnight on Monday. It is now a Special Administrative Region to be governed under a mini-constitution, the Basic Law.
Under the Basic Law Beijing will handle matters relating to Hong Kong's defence and foreign relations but allow the region a high degree of autonomy in handling all other matters.
"The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government is also authorised to handle relevant external affairs on its own," said Qian at the opening ceremony. He did not elaborate.
Ma thanked everyone involved in the project, especially Li Ka Shing and Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd.
Cheung Kong built the headquarters which sits just above the central business district in an area formerly occupied by government housing for single civil servants in the British colonial government.
